title: A Quantitative Description of Membrane Current and Its Application to Conduction and Excitation in Nerve
core_idea: Coupled differential equations reproducing the action potential from ion-channel dynamics.
why_it_matters: Proof that computation can be *derived* from biophysics — the template for mechanistic explanation that AI's interpretability now imitates.

title: Receptive Fields, Binocular Interaction and Functional Architecture in the Cat's Visual Cortex
core_idea: Cortical neurons are arranged in hierarchical feature detectors — simple cells feed complex cells with invariance.
why_it_matters: The direct biological inspiration for CNNs (LeCun 1989) — hierarchy + feature + invariance was observed in cortex 27 years before AlexNet.

title: The Hippocampus as a Cognitive Map
link: Oxford University Press (book; place cells: O'Keefe & Dostrovsky 1971)
core_idea: Place cells encode location; hippocampus implements a map-like relational memory, not a warehouse.
why_it_matters: Memory as structured, relational, spatial — the design reference for vector stores, agent spatial reasoning, and episodic memory architectures.

title: Vision: A Computational Investigation into the Human Representation and Processing of Visual Information
core_idea: Any intelligent system must be understood at three levels — computation (what/why), algorithm (how), implementation (substrate) — and levels are separable.
why_it_matters: The discipline that keeps AI honest: transformer = one algorithmic answer; LLM scaling debates are arguments at Marr's computational level.

title: Reactivation of Hippocampal Ensemble Memories During Sleep
core_idea: Sequences of place-cell activity from waking experience are replayed during sleep.
why_it_matters: Offline consolidation as a computation — the biological justification for experience replay in RL (DQN) and for offline training phases generally.

title: Emergence of Simple-Cell Receptive Field Properties by Learning a Sparse Code for Natural Images
core_idea: Optimizing for SPARSE codes of natural images reproduces V1 receptive fields — no teacher, no labels.
why_it_matters: The brain's sensory code is shaped by efficient coding of environmental statistics; the direct ancestor of sparse autoencoder features in LLM interpretability (domain 03, F8).

title: A Neural Substrate of Prediction and Reward (dopamine neurons)
authors: Wolfram Schultz, Peter Dayan, Read Montague
core_idea: Dopamine neurons do not signal reward — they signal REWARD PREDICTION ERROR, exactly the TD error of Q-learning.
why_it_matters: The single most celebrated neuro↔AI bridge: a learning algorithm (TD, domain 02) was discovered in neurons before it was standard in machines (or rather, matched after) — reward prediction errors drive both.

title: Predictive Coding in the Visual Cortex: A Functional Interpretation of Some Extra-Classical Receptive-Field Effects
core_idea: Cortex transmits prediction ERRORS up the hierarchy (feedback carries predictions); explains end-stopping and contextual effects.
why_it_matters: Bandwidth-efficient, learned, hierarchical inference — the brain runs a self-supervised predictive model; the blueprint for predictive-processing architectures and a candidate biologically plausible learning rule.

title: A Neural Global Workspace Theory of Conscious (and Unconscious) Processing
authors: Stanislas Dehaene, Jean-Pierre Changeux (building on Baars' Global Workspace 1988)
link: https://doi.org/10.1016/S1053-8119(03)00067-7 (with Baars 2003 Neuron: "A neuronal global workspace model")
core_idea: Conscious access = broadcasting of a winner-take-all selection through a global workspace — a shared, capacity-limited bottleneck routed to many processors.
why_it_matters: A concrete architecture pattern (bottleneck + broadcast) that inspired MoE-style routing, LLM context as workspace, and modular agent designs (Goyal & Bengio 2020).

title: An Information-Theoretic Measure of Consciousness (Integrated Information Theory)
core_idea: Consciousness corresponds to integrated information (Φ) — the causal irreducibility of a system's parts.
why_it_matters: Influential formal program linking substrate structure to experience; CONTested (adversarial testing 2023 favored recurrent processing over IIT) — include as theory-design lesson: formal elegance ≠ empirical validity.

title: Neuronal Circuits of the Neocortex: The Canonical Microcircuit
core_idea: Cortex is a repeated canonical circuit (6 layers, characteristic recurrence and inhibition) whose connectivity is stereotyped across areas.
why_it_matters: Nature's answer to architecture reuse: one repeated block, specialized by input/output, prefigures layer-stacking universality (transformer blocks).

title: Microstructure of a Spatial Map in the Entorhinal Cortex (grid cells)
authors: Torkel Hafting, Marianne Fyhn, Sturla Molden, May-Britt Moser, Edvard Moser
core_idea: Entorhinal grid cells fire on hexagonal tessellations — a metric spatial code.
why_it_matters: Nobel-recognized discovery of an elegant internal coordinate system; grid-cell-like codes emerge in RL agents (Banino 2018) — convergent evolution of representation between brains and networks.

title: Uncertainty, Neuromodulation, and Attention (ACh & NE)
core_idea: Acetylcholine signals expected uncertainty; norepinephrine signals unexpected uncertainty — neuromodulators encode uncertainty types, gating learning and attention.
why_it_matters: Global state control as architecture: neuromodulation is a broadcast hyperparameter system — the biological template for meta-learners, adaptive optimizers, and context conditioning in ML.

title: Small-World Brain Networks
core_idea: Human brain graphs combine high local clustering with short global path lengths — optimal for segregated AND integrated processing.
why_it_matters: Network-architecture lesson for AI: mixture-of-experts routing, agent topologies, and MoE load-balancing are engineering rediscoveries of small-world design.

title: Neuronal Avalanches in Neocortical Circuits
link: https://doi.org/10.1523/JNEUROSCI.23-35-11167.2003 (J. Neurosci. 2003); see also Kinouchi & Copelli 2006, Nat. Phys.
core_idea: Cortical activity propagates in power-law-distributed avalanches — signatures of operation near a critical point.
why_it_matters: Evidence the brain self-tunes to criticality (maximal dynamic range, information transmission) — matching self-organized criticality in physics (domain 01, F11) and edge-of-chaos results in RNN/attention dynamics.

title: Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA): Connecting Computational Models with Brains
authors: Nikolaus Kriegeskorte, Marieke Mur, Peter Bandettini
link: https://doi.org/10.3389/neuro.06.039.2008 (Frontiers in Systems Neuroscience; concept formalizing Edelman 1998)
core_idea: Compare representations via geometry of pairwise distances — model-agnostic comparison between brains, behavior, and machines.
why_it_matters: The measurement tool of representational convergence: CNN layers ↔ visual cortex correspondences (later Yamins et al. 2014) were established this way; reusable for comparing your model's internal geometry to anything.

title: Sleep and Synaptic Homeostasis
core_idea: Sleep globally downscales synaptic strengths — renormalizing after a day of potentiation, preserving relative weights.
why_it_matters: A biological analogue of normalization and weight decay — "forget the noise, keep the signal"; a design hint for continual-learning systems that consolidate by re-normalizing.

title: Prioritized Memory Access Reveals Planning Networks in the Brain
core_idea: What to replay is itself a computation: expected reward gain × shortcut-to-decision determine replay priority.
why_it_matters: Explains WHY experience replay works and when: prioritized replay is information-theoretically optimal curriculum — directly transferable to RL buffer design and agent memory management.

title: Dendritic Error Backpropagation in Deep Cortical Microcircuits
authors: João Sacramento, Rui Ponte Costa, Yoshua Bengio, Walter Senn
core_idea: Layer-specific dendritic compartments can carry error signals locally, approximating backprop in a biologically plausible cortical circuit.
why_it_matters: Existence proof that error-driven deep learning might be implementable in wetware — and a template for local-learning-rule hardware (neuromorphic, optical).

title: Random Feedback Weights Support Learning in Deep Neural Networks (feedback alignment)
authors: Timothy Lillicrap, Daniel Cownden, Douglas Tweed, Colin Akerman
core_idea: Backward weights need not be symmetric — networks adapt their forward weights to whatever feedback channel exists.
why_it_matters: Kills the "backprop is biologically impossible" objection in its simplest form; enables training on hardware where exact reverse passes are impractical.

title: Towards an Integration of Deep Learning and Neuroscience
authors: Adam Marblestone, Greg Wayne, Konrad Kording
core_idea: Systematic map of what neuroscience could contribute to deep learning: memory, attention, continual learning — with the transfer direction specified.
why_it_matters: The reference agenda for neuro→AI borrowing; use as a checklist against your architecture design.

title: Neuroscience-Inspired Artificial Intelligence
authors: Demis Hassabis, Dharshan Kumaran, Courtney Summerfield, Matthew Botvinick
core_idea: Historical and forward synthesis: reliving the neuro→AI pipeline that produced CNNs/RL/attention, and what remains untapped (meta-learning, memory consolidation).
why_it_matters: The manifesto of the field from DeepMind's cofounder — argues AGI likely requires re-engagement with brain mechanisms.

title: Prefrontal Cortex as a Meta-Reinforcement Learning System
authors: Jane Wang, Zeb Kurth-Nelson, Dharshan Kumaran, ... Matthew Botvinick, Demis Hassabis
core_idea: The brain's prefrontal system implements meta-RL: slow synaptic learning (outside) shapes a fast in-context learner (inside) — and the same dynamics emerge in recurrent ANNs trained on task distributions.
why_it_matters: Unifies biological and artificial in-context learning: prefrontal meta-RL ≈ transformer ICL (domain 03, F7); tells you when learned recurrent state beats weight updates.

title: High-Dimensional Geometry of Population Responses
authors: Stringer, C. et al. (Carsen Stringer, Marius Pachitariu, Nicholas Steinmetz, ... Kenneth Harris)
link: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1346-5 ("High-dimensional geometry of population responses in visual cortex", Nature)
core_idea: Cortical populations track many stimulus variables (near-power-law eigenspectrum) while remaining decodable — high-dimensional but smooth, no collapse.
why_it_matters: Empirical geometry that neural networks should match; connects to superposition (domain 03, F8) and neural collapse (domain 01) — three views of representation geometry across substrates.

title: Inductive Biases for Higher-Level Cognition
core_idea: Transplant Global-Workspace-style inductive biases (bottleneck, modules, broadcast, attention control) into deep nets for combinatorial generalization.
why_it_matters: The most concrete GWT-to-architecture pipeline — directly relevant to modular/multi-agent LLM system design (domain 05).

title: A Survey on Neuro-Mimetic Deep Learning via Predictive Coding
link: arXiv (2025; PubMed-indexed — search "Salvatori predictive coding survey")
core_idea: Comprehensive survey of predictive coding as a learning algorithm — approximating backprop with local errors, with efficiency gains on edge hardware.
why_it_matters: The 2025 state of a serious backprop alternative: local, online, event-friendly — candidate learning rule for neuromorphic and continually-learning systems (domain 05).
